title: Review of c45's dense sink escape: Supported for the escape advantage (fresh seed 97: 21/35 at mar 40 vs 6/30 at mar 0) and the longer per-cycle swim in S (median D 2.33 vs 1.69 in I); the selection-gradient clause is untestable on this seed because dense discs leave only 4 rods with a descendant count in S
summary: Re-ran the sink-disc world with one disc per 50 t on seed 97, T=1600, in arms S, I and S at mar 0, with c00's extract.py and the finding's fate.py unchanged. S, mar 40: 35 bodies caught, 21 escape, 14 dissolve (0.60); 16 persistent splits; 6 dividing tracks, median D 2.33 rod lengths, 3 with D >= 3; only 4 enter the selection regression, so no gradient is reported. I, mar 40: 2 caught; 17 persistent splits; 12 dividing tracks, median D 1.69; D gradient -0.030 [-0.271, +0.323], path speed +0.205, straightness -0.115 (n=12). S, mar 0: 30 caught, 6 escape (0.20); 12 persistent splits; 4 dividing tracks, median D 0.86, path speed 0.047.

observations.M: S_s97/fate.txt vs S_mar0_s97/fate.txt: escape 21/35 (0.60) vs 6/30 (0.20); dividing rods in S median D 2.33 (3 of 6 with D >= 3) vs 1.69 in I and 0.86 at mar 0

seeds_run.result: pass for the escape advantage and longer swims in S; selection gradient not testable (n=4 in S)

controls_run.M: S_mar0_s97/ (mar 0) and I_s97/ (removal arm), same seed and disc stream

verdicts.limitation: Dense discs cut division hard on this seed (6 dividing tracks in S, 4 at mar 0), so per-arm trait statistics rest on a handful of rods and the claim that escape cancels the swim cost (gradient +0.02 in S vs -0.32 in I) could not be checked; in my removal arm the D gradient is not negative (-0.03, CI spans 0). I did not run mtips.py, so the translation clause is not checked by me (the sheet shows rods leaving discs whole).
